Monitoring shows degraded performance across multiple services.

We are observing CORS errors when the frontend communicates with backend APIs.

complete_message: We're experiencing a major disruption to our continuous integration platform: customers cannot access the web interface or trigger new builds, and we're seeing degraded performance across multiple services. The issue started around 00:16 UTC, with monitoring also showing a drop in code-hosting webhooks, widespread frontend-to-backend connectivity problems, and CORS errors. We haven't identified a trigger yet, and although we were just wrapping up another incident, we've established that this is a separate issue.

It's our continuous integration platform. Both the web interface and the ability to trigger new builds are affected.

conversation.analyst: The disruption started around 00:16 UTC, and our monitoring detected degraded performance between 00:26 and 00:52 UTC. Customers are unable to access the interface or start builds, and multiple services are affected, but we don't have a confirmed regional or percentage breakdown.

We're seeing widespread connectivity problems between our frontend and backend APIs, including CORS errors. Monitoring also shows degraded performance across multiple services and a drop in incoming webhooks from our code-hosting provider.

discovered_later.root_cause: An operator inadvertently modified a Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule while investigating routine security monitoring, believing the actions were read-only. A misconfiguration in IAM permissions allowed the operator's role to modify infrastructure directly, bypassing the standard Terraform deployment process. The modified rule blocked legitimate traffic to two CDN distributions serving the platform's web interface and API. Because the change occurred outside Terraform, investigators initially had no corresponding deployment record and did not prioritize investigating the WAF configuration. Automated Terraform drift detection eventually identified the unauthorized configuration difference approximately 80 minutes after the initial change.
fix: At 01:35 UTC, automated Terraform drift detection identified the difference between the expected and actual WAF configurations.
At 01:41 UTC, the engineering team reverted the problematic WAF rule on both affected CDN distributions.
At 01:49 UTC, monitoring confirmed that error rates were decreasing across affected services as legitimate traffic was routed correctly again.
At 01:55 UTC, full service restoration was confirmed.
prevention: Implemented stricter IAM policies to prevent direct modification of infrastructure managed through the infrastructure-as-code pipeline.
Enhancing Terraform drift detection to provide faster alerts when critical infrastructure configurations differ from their expected state.
Adding technical guardrails to ensure infrastructure configuration changes follow the standard infrastructure-as-code process.
Establishing improved protocols for implementing and testing WAF rules before production deployment.
Adding monitoring specifically for WAF behavior and traffic patterns to detect similar disruptions more quickly.
Investigating organization-wide Security Control Policies (SCPs) to restrict IAM role permissions and prevent unauthorized changes to critical infrastructure.
discovered_later.changes: The immediate configuration correction was the reversal of an inadvertently modified WAF rule on two CDN distributions. Stricter IAM policies were subsequently implemented to restrict direct infrastructure modifications. Additional Terraform drift-detection improvements, WAF monitoring, configuration guardrails, and security-policy restrictions were identified as ongoing or planned improvements. No application code changes were reported.
